title: Fourier coefficient at a leading coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a subset of the last $n$ coordinates, identified with the coordinates of $\{\pm1\}^n$. The Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the frequency consisting of coordinate $0$ together with the corresponding coordinates in $S$ is one half the difference between the Fourier coefficients at $S$ of the two slices obtained by fixing coordinate $0$ to $1$ and to $-1$, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean cube
$S$ is a subset of the $n$ tail coordinates
